project.commit_note: The exact staged checkout inspected under `gt_results/arvo_393401458/_work/src/grok` is commit `87e10814f24cdad5f33d8f3786fa97a44cf1b6bd`, which is an ancestor of the metadata vulnerable commit `aa61ec44fa8ef6774b8573a02b0070c8485eaaee`. It still contains the same vulnerable include-tracker logic and matches the saved ASan line map at `src/lib/core/t2/PacketIter.h:81,126,131` and `src/lib/core/t2/PacketIter.cpp:625,845`.

classification.classification_note: AddressSanitizer reports a 1-byte read past a 1024-byte lazily allocated include-tracker chunk in `src/lib/core/t2/PacketIter.h:131`.

bug_description.original: OSS-Fuzz issue 393401458 (grok): Heap-buffer-overflow READ 1 found by fuzz target grk_decompress_fuzzer [asan].
bug_description.normalized: Stage 01 reproduced AddressSanitizer at `src/lib/core/t2/PacketIter.h:131` while Grok decoded the staged 135-byte raw JPEG 2000 codestream (`gt_results/arvo_393401458/poc`, sha256 `680607a418ae2a7898fa8e2d3558b345fafcf34b70bf5a0cc4b6d9ee2b70cd6d`). The witness main header first makes `read_cod()` consume the COD `Scod` byte `0x01` at offset `0x37` from the `FF52` marker that begins at offset `0x33`; the following `SGcod(A)` progression-order byte at offset `0x38` is `0x03`. `read_cod()` then propagates `tcp->csty & J2K_CCP_CSTY_PRT` into `tccp->csty`, which lets `read_SPCod_SPCoc()` take the custom-precinct branch, materialize `tccp->numresolutions == 6`, and parse six precinct-exponent bytes. `read_poc()` then appends two progression-order-change entries from the `FF5F` POC marker, with the first appended entry carrying `Ppoc = 0x04` (`GRK_CPRL`). `PacketManager::getParams()` converts the parsed resolution/precinct state into `numPrecinctsPerRes[resno]`, and `PacketIter::init()` later disables the single-progression shortcut and selects the CPRL iterator whose stack frame is saved in the crash log. On that path, `next_cprl()` computes a `precinctIndex`, `update_include()` forwards the current packet coordinates into `IncludeTracker::update`, and `get_include()` asks `ResIncludeBuffers::get_byte()` for the last byte of the include bitmap so the chunk exists. `get_byte()` therefore returns a pointer already advanced to that selected byte inside a 1024-byte chunk, but vulnerable `IncludeTracker::update` still recomputes `include_index = (compno * numprecs + precno) >> 3` and reads `include[include_index]` as if the pointer were the start of the bitmap. That double-applies the byte offset and produces the saved `heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 1`, which ASan places 466 bytes past the 1024-byte chunk allocated in `ResIncludeBuffers::get_byte`. The staged fix commit removes this second indexing by updating the selected byte directly inside the per-layer include buffer.

evidence_note: The saved vulnerable run and ASan trace pin the crash site, allocation site, and caller chain. They do not print the exact crashing `(pino, compno, resno, precinctIndex)` tuple, so the trace keeps those iterator coordinates symbolic and only attributes source-level facts established by the staged source, PoC bytes, patch, and crash evidence. `runtime_disambiguation` is disabled for this sample, so no instrumentation was added.

source.description: First vulnerability-relevant project-code read on the crashing path. The COD handler consumes the attacker's `Scod` byte and materializes the custom-precinct style bits that are later copied into `tccp->csty` and checked before Grok parses attacker-controlled precinct exponents.
source.value_from: In the staged 135-byte codestream, the `FF52 0012` COD marker starts at offset `0x33`. Its `Scod` byte at offset `0x37` is `0x01`, while the following `SGcod(A)` progression-order byte at offset `0x38` is `0x03`; because `J2K_CP_CSTY_PRT` is `0x01`, this step sets the custom-precinct flag that reaches the vulnerable path.

root_cause.description: Root cause. `include` is already the byte pointer returned by `get_include()`/`get_byte()`, but `update()` still treats it as a base array and indexes by `include_index` again. No rebasing or direct-byte access corrects that second offset; the staged fix removes this extra indexing and updates the selected byte directly.

sink.description: ASan crash site. The first read from `include[include_index]` goes past the 1024-byte chunk that `ResIncludeBuffers::get_byte()` allocated and triggers the saved heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 1.
sink.note: The saved trace reports address `0x519000011952`, which is 466 bytes beyond the 1024-byte region `[0x519000011380,0x519000011780)` allocated at `src/lib/core/t2/PacketIter.h:81`.

tainted_value_origin.description: This is the first exact materialization of the packet-grid size that later reaches the sink. The parsed COD/SPCod state is converted into a per-resolution precinct count, and that count is cached in `IncludeTracker` as the stride reused by both `len = numprecs * numcomps + 7` and `index = compno * numprecs + precno`.
tainted_value_origin.value_from: The `precinctGridWidth`/`precinctGridHeight` inputs here are derived from the staged witness's parsed `tccp->numresolutions` and `tccp->precWidthExp[]`/`precHeightExp[]` fields.
tainted_value_origin.note: Later iterator logic keeps `compno` and `precinctIndex` symbolic, but this stored `num_precincts` value is the shared quantity that links the parsed header geometry to the overflowing include-bitmap access.

parser_admitted.description: The witness main header is admitted far enough that Grok enters the COD parser and starts consuming the style byte that enables the downstream custom-precinct parsing and packet-iterator state.
parser_admitted.note: The saved PoC is recognized as a JPEG 2000 codestream by `file(1)`, and the staged source reaches this read before any Tier-2 packet iteration begins.

coarse_trace.summary: The COD parser reads `Scod` and propagates the custom-precinct bit into each tile-component coding style.
The SPCod parser reads the witness resolution count and, because `tccp->csty` requests custom precincts, consumes six precinct-exponent bytes.
The POC parser appends two progression-order-change entries; the first appended entry carries `GRK_CPRL`, which later yields the crashing `next_cprl` iterator.
PacketManager converts the parsed header state into per-resolution precinct-grid sizes and caches `numPrecinctsPerRes` inside `IncludeTracker`.
Packet iterator initialization disables the single-progression shortcut and selects the POC-provided CPRL progression for the iterator instance that later crashes.
The CPRL iterator reaches a valid packet, derives a `precinctIndex`, and forwards the current layer/resolution/component/precinct coordinates into `update_include()`.

`IncludeTracker::update` obtains a pointer already offset to the last include-bitmap byte, recomputes a second byte index from packet coordinates, and reads `include[include_index]`, causing the saved heap-buffer-overflow.

fine_trace.note: Source. `read_cod()` reads the witness `Scod` byte `0x01` at offset `0x37` into `tcp->csty`; the next COD byte `0x03` at offset `0x38` is the separate `SGcod(A)` progression-order field. Because `J2K_CP_CSTY_PRT` is `0x01`, the `Scod` byte carries the custom-precinct flag that later governs whether attacker-controlled precinct bytes are parsed.

fine_trace.code:
for(i = 0; i < image->numcomps; ++i)
   tcp->tccps[i].csty = tcp->csty & J2K_CCP_CSTY_PRT;
fine_trace.note: The COD handler propagates the custom-precinct bit into every tile-component coding style. On the component state that `read_SPCod_SPCoc()` receives, `tccp->csty` becomes nonzero, which is the exact flag checked before any precinct bytes are consumed.

Using the same component coding-parameter block from step 2, the SPCod parser reads the witness decomposition-count byte `0x05` and increments it to `tccp->numresolutions == 6`. That resolution count later bounds both the custom precinct-byte loop and the packet-grid derivation.

Because step 2 left `tccp->csty & J2K_CCP_CSTY_PRT` nonzero and step 3 produced `tccp->numresolutions == 6`, `read_SPCod_SPCoc()` takes the custom-precinct branch instead of the default-exponent branch. The remaining header bytes satisfy the size check, so parsing proceeds into the six-byte loop.

Inside that branch, the loop consumes `tccp->numresolutions` precinct bytes and splits each byte into low-nibble width and high-nibble height exponents. For the staged witness, the six parsed bytes are `20 ff ff ff ff ff` at offsets `0x41`-`0x46` of the codestream.

The POC parser first derives `maxNumResLevels` from the already-parsed `tccp->numresolutions`, then consumes two 7-byte progression entries from the witness `FF5F 0010` marker. Because `oldNumProgressions` is 1, the first appended entry lands at `progressionOrderChange[1]`; its `Ppoc` byte is `0x04`, so this step stores `GRK_CPRL` there and, after both entries, sets `tcp->numpocs = 2`.

Using the parsed resolution count and precinct exponents, `getParams()` computes each resolution's precinct-grid extent for every component. The resulting `num_precincts` is cached as `numPrecinctsPerRes[resno]`, which later becomes the shared stride in both `len = numprecs * numcomps + 7` and `index = compno * numprecs + precno`.

The include-tracker fast path is disabled here. Step 6 made `tcp->numpocs = 2`, so `packetManager->getNumProgressions()` returns 3 and `singleProgression_` becomes false. Later `update_include()` therefore calls the include tracker instead of returning early.

For each iterator instance, decompression uses the matching POC entry whenever `tcp->hasPoc()` is true. The saved crash stack proves the crashing iterator selected a `GRK_CPRL` entry here, because `next_cprl()` is the immediate caller of `update_include()`.

Inside `next_cprl()`, after `validatePrecinct()` accepts the current component/resolution packet and `layno < prog.lay_e` holds, the iterator turns the current packet-grid coordinates into a linear precinct number. This value is the precinct-side operand later folded into `index = compno * numprecs + precno`.
Because step 8 left `singleProgression_` false, the fast path is skipped and the current layer/resolution/component/precinct coordinates are forwarded into `IncludeTracker::update()`.

The include tracker converts the stored per-resolution precinct count into the logical size of the include bitmap for this resolution/layer pair. By asking `get_byte()` for `len - 1`, it intentionally materializes the last byte of that bitmap rather than a base pointer.

The last-bit request from step 12 is converted into a byte position inside a 1024-byte chunk. If that chunk does not exist, this path allocates it, and the returned pointer is already advanced by `offset` bytes into that chunk. ASan's allocation stack names this exact `new uint8_t[GRK_INCLUDE_TRACKER_CHUNK_SIZE]()` site.

Root cause. The current packet coordinates are folded into a second byte index `include_index`, but `include` is already the selected-byte pointer returned by step 13, not the start of the bitmap. Treating it as `include[include_index]` therefore double-applies the byte offset. The staged fix removes this second indexing and updates the selected byte directly.

Sink. This first read uses the already-offset pointer from step 13 plus the rederived `include_index` from step 14, so it lands at `0x519000011952`, 466 bytes beyond the 1024-byte region `[0x519000011380,0x519000011780)`. AddressSanitizer reports `heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 1` at this exact line with stack `update -> update_include -> grk::PacketIter::next_cprl`.

format.name: JPEG 2000 codestream
format.contract: The staged trigger is the exact 135-byte raw JPEG 2000 codestream in `gt_results/arvo_393401458/poc` (sha256 `680607a418ae2a7898fa8e2d3558b345fafcf34b70bf5a0cc4b6d9ee2b70cd6d`). Its main header contains the COD bytes `ff 52 00 12 01 03 20 20 01 05 04 04 20 01 20 ff ff ff ff ff ff`, beginning at offset `0x33`, where `Scod = 0x01` at `0x37` makes `read_cod()` set the custom-precinct flag and the following `SGcod(A)` progression-order byte is `0x03` at `0x38`; `SPcod(D) = 0x05` makes `read_SPCod_SPCoc()` materialize `tccp->numresolutions == 6`, and the six subsequent precinct bytes are `20 ff ff ff ff ff`. It also contains the POC bytes `ff 5f 00 10 00 00 00 02 20 20 04 00 00 20 20 20 20 02`, whose first appended entry carries `Ppoc = 0x04` (`GRK_CPRL`). This contract is limited to those exact staged bytes and the source-level fields they populate on the crashing path; it does not generalize beyond the witnessed codestream.
